chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz, from Muhammad ibn Muslim who said:

I asked him (peace be upon him) about grains — which of them are subject to zakat? He said: Wheat, barley, corn, millet, rice, hulless barley (sult), lentils, and sesame — all of these are subject to zakat, and those resembling them.

key_terms.أَشْبَاهُهُ: those resembling it — extends the zakat ruling by analogy to crops similar in nature to the listed eight
key_terms.السُّلْت: sult — a variety of barley without husk, sometimes identified as a type of rye; a classical agricultural term
key_terms.الْحُبُوب: grains — the category of agricultural produce under discussion for zakat obligation
key_terms.يُزَكَّى: is subject to zakat — literally 'is purified'; paying zakat is described as purification of wealth

ai.seo_question: Which grains are obligatorily subject to zakat in Shia Islam according to Al-Kafi?
ai.summary: This hadith establishes which agricultural grains are obligatorily subject to zakat (the Islamic alms-tax) according to Imam al-Sadiq (AS). The Imam enumerates eight specific grains: wheat, barley, corn, millet, rice, sult (a type of hulless barley), lentils, and sesame, and extends the ruling to anything similar in nature. This ruling forms a foundational legal precedent in Shia jurisprudence for agricultural zakat obligations.
